```{r}
#| label: library

options(housepi.footer.sample = TRUE)
library(housepi)
housepi_theme_set()
set.seed(42)
```

Contact rates allow modelling differential transmission between groups of individuals within a household.
Unlike group rates, which apply to a single individual, contact rates define pairwise from/to relationships.
We illustrate the API using the Matsumoto influenza household survey.

# Define a contact rate

We start by loading the chain binomial model and the `flu_2014_matsumoto` dataset.
This dataset contains household reports of influenza episodes with a `member` column distinguishing different household member categories. 
To simplify this walkthrough, we consider only 2 categories: "child" and "adult":

```{r}
#| label: load-model-data
# simplify 
dataset <- flu_2014_matsumoto |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    member = dplyr::case_when(
      member == "student" ~ "child",
      member == "sibling" ~ "child",
      .default = "adult"
    )
  )

# inspect the data
head(dataset)

# define a chain binomial model and load parameter template
hhmodel <- dataset |>
  new_housepi_model("chain_binomial") |>
  add_parameter_template()
```

Use `add_contact_rate()` to define pairwise transmission rates based on a categorical feature.
This creates from/to parameter pairs for each combination of groups.

```{r}
#| label: add-contact-rate
# define symmetric contact rates automatically
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_rate("member") |>
  get_contact_rates()

# asymmetric case
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_rate("member", symmetric = FALSE) |>
  get_contact_rates()
```

Each row in the output represents a directed from/to pair.
The `param_name` column gives the corresponding parameter that will scale the transmission rate between those groups. 
If not stated differently, the contact is assumed symmetric, which implies that pairs from/to and to/from share the same parameter. 
Parameters generated by the contact rate follow the same MCMC defaults as in group rates.
Their generic definition can be provided as shown in [Group rates](group_rates.html).

# Specify a custom reference pair

The `.reference` pair (by default the most frequent combination) is fixed at 1.
Provide a `reference` to select which from/to pair acts as the baseline:

```{r}
#| label: custom-reference
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_rate(
    by = "member",
    reference = c(from_member = "child", to_member = "child")
  ) |>
  get_contact_rates()
```

A convenience shorthand applies the same reference value to both from and to:
e.g. passing `reference = c(member = "child")` is equivalent to the previous.
